Amir —

Thanks for the snapshot. High level answers up front: yes, we can place a 30-day temporary hold (soft lock) on a dedicated slice and convert to a reserved pool on signature. The temporary hold preserves node affinity and capacity headroom but does not commit billing until you convert. Operationally:

- Soft hold: earmark a set of GPU slots (node IDs) and mark them as unavailable for new on-demand allocations; allowed for 30 days.
- Conversion: convert the hold to Reserved (monthly billing) with 7-day activation window for billing start.
- Burst: held capacity allows limited burst above baseline if you enable burst credits (subject to capacity at time).

I pushed an initial sizing workbook (fleet-sizing-sheet.xlsx) with two scenarios — conservative and stretch — keyed to your 95th percentile QPS. Ben, can you confirm the node topology (vCPU/RAM/GPU type) assumptions?

Marissa, can you estimate how a partially-quantized runtime (8-bit activations) changes unit cost and any SLO impact?

Next step: Amir, if you confirm which scenario you prefer we’ll propose the hold amount and issue a soft-hold notice to ops.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Looping in ops flavor:

Quick read of the conservative scenario in the workbook — it assumes T4-equivalent nodes (16GB GPU mem) with 20% KV-cache headroom. For Galaxykite's 95th-percentile, that maps to ~12 nodes (slice) for baseline and 18 nodes for stretch.

Operational constraints:
- Soft-hold: we can mark 12 nodes as soft-held today. That will remove them from the general allocation pool; they remain in a stand-by assignment state.
- Scheduling: soft-held nodes can still serve if explicitly targeted by tenant routing (your routes). Burst above baseline will only be permitted up to 20% of capacity and requires a preconfigured burst policy.
- Timeline: ops needs a signed soft-hold memo to file; actual node-affinity tagging happens within 24hrs of the request.

Risks/notes:
- If other late-stage deals request overlapping physical racks, we'll prioritize based on deal stage and committed MRR. We should add a conservative buffer of 2 nodes to reduce collision risk.
- Partial quantization primarily affects GPU memory pressure; if Galaxykite adopts 8-bit LLM runtimes we can likely get one fewer node in baseline but may need performance testing to validate latency SLOs.

Karthik — can you confirm we have spare rack margin in us-west-2 for the 30d window starting 2029-05-01? If not, we'll ask for a slightly later activation.

-Ben
Head of Capacity Planning
Redwood Inference

Amir / team —

Checked infra availability for us-west-2 (candidate racks): we have a 15-node spare pool in the relevant capacity zones for the May 1 start. I can approve a 30-day soft hold for up to 14 nodes starting 2029-05-01, provided Galaxykite signs the soft-hold acknowledgement (one-page doc) and agrees to the activation window. Please note the operational terms in the attached memo: soft-hold preserves placement but not billing; we reserve the right to preempt if a higher-priority committed order arrives but will provide 72-hour notice.

Amir — if you want to proceed with the conservative scenario, we recommend booking 14 nodes (12 baseline + 2 buffer) to avoid cross-deal contention. Once you confirm, Stephanie will generate the soft-hold memo and ops will tag the nodes.

Karthik Iyer
